scope.question: What are the reactor-CEvNS and cosmic-ray-muon differential rate spectra in reconstructed energy for a 1 kg monolithic Ge crystal read out by QPDs with Ta->Al and Al->Hf trapping designs?
in_scope: Reactor CEvNS differential rate spectrum in reconstructed energy for a 3 GWth commercial reactor at 25 m standoff with a 4-isotope Huber-Mueller-like antineutrino spectrum
Sea-level cosmic-ray muon energy-deposit spectrum in reconstructed energy for a single monolithic 1 kg Ge crystal

Detector response model: deposited energy to ~50% signal efficiency, trapped quasiparticle number, EMG-profiled tunneling burst, 50 kHz bandwidth-limited reconstruction with perfect tunneling identification
Both trapping designs: Ta absorber to Al trap/junction and Al absorber to Hf trap/junction
QPD sensor density of 1 per mm^2 on the crystal surface
out_of_scope: G4CMP phonon-transport simulation (deferred to a later stage)
Imperfect quasiparticle-tunneling identification and readout-noise modeling
unresolved_questions: What crystal area is instrumented (one face vs all faces), fixing N_sens from the 1/mm^2 sensor density?
How should reconstruction behave in the saturated regime: simple Nyquist rate-clip or a dead-time model?
How should the Ta->Al device tunneling parameters be mapped from the QPD paper's tabulated Al- and Hf-junction devices?

known_good_baselines: J. Billard et al., J. Phys. G 44, 105101 (2017), arXiv:1612.09035 (Ge CEvNS reactor rate predictions)
Particle Data Group Review of Particle Physics: sea-level muon flux of about 1 muon per cm^2 per minute
context_gaps: Instrumented surface area and per-sensor energy split for the 1 kg crystal not yet fixed
Ta->Al device tunneling parameters (K, Gamma_out, tau_qp) not tabulated in the QPD paper
crucial_inputs: 100% phonon collection with ~50% overall deposited-energy-to-signal efficiency
50 kHz signal bandwidth: tunneling faster than the ~25 kHz Nyquist rate is unresolvable
Perfect identification of quasiparticle tunneling events
QPD sensor density of 1 per mm^2
Commercial 3 GWth reactor at 25 m standoff
Sea-level muon flux with no overburden
Exponentially-modified-Gaussian pulse template from the qpd repo

formulations: Freedman CEvNS differential cross section with Helm form factor on natural Ge folded with a 4-isotope reactor antineutrino spectrum
Analytic and Monte-Carlo response chain from deposited energy to bandwidth-limited reconstructed energy using the QPD paper pulse model and the qpd-repo EMG template
allowed_estimator_families: Direct spectrum folding and Monte-Carlo sampling of the response chain
allowed_fit_families: EMG pulse-template fits for energy reconstruction
stop_and_rethink_conditions: The CEvNS reconstructed spectrum falls entirely below the effective threshold for both designs
Muon-induced pileup at sea level makes quiescent reconstruction impossible at 50 kHz bandwidth

observables.name: Reactor CEvNS differential rate spectrum
observables.definition: Differential CEvNS event rate versus reconstructed energy for the 1 kg Ge QPD detector

observables.name: Cosmic-ray muon spectrum
observables.definition: Differential cosmic-ray muon event rate versus reconstructed energy for the same detector

observables.name: Energy response curve
observables.definition: Reconstructed energy versus deposited energy per trapping design, including 50 kHz bandwidth saturation

claims.statement: The reactor CEvNS spectrum in reconstructed energy is computed for both trapping designs and its total rate agrees with published Ge reactor predictions within a factor of about 2

The sea-level muon spectrum in reconstructed energy is computed for both designs with the bandwidth-saturation regime made explicit, and the integral muon rate matches the PDG sea-level flux through the crystal
The reconstructed-versus-deposited energy response, including saturation from the 25 kHz maximum resolvable tunneling rate, is derived for both trapping designs

deliverables.description: CEvNS and muon differential rate spectra versus reconstructed energy for both trapping designs
Reconstructed versus deposited energy response with the saturation onset marked
Python implementation of the CEvNS and muon spectrum calculation and the QPD response pipeline
must_contain: response chain from deposited to reconstructed energy

deliverables.description: Assumptions and results note for the stage-1 rough estimate

acceptance_tests.subject: claim-cevns
acceptance_tests.procedure: Compare the integrated CEvNS rate above threshold against the Ge reactor predictions of Billard et al. (2017), rescaled to 3 GWth at 25 m

acceptance_tests.subject: claim-muon
acceptance_tests.procedure: Integrate the muon event rate through the crystal and compare with the PDG sea-level flux times the crystal geometric acceptance

acceptance_tests.subject: claim-response
acceptance_tests.procedure: Check the low-energy limit (reconstructed energy equals 0.5 times deposited energy within statistical scatter) and the high-energy limit (response saturates once the tunneling rate exceeds 25 kHz)
acceptance_tests.pass_condition: Both limiting behaviors reproduced by the pipeline

references.locator: K. Ramanathan et al., APS Open Science 1, 000013 (2026), DOI 10.1103/kqd2-spb1
references.why_it_matters: Defines the QPD detection concept, efficiency chain, pulse model, and Table II device parameters
Canonical exponentially-modified-Gaussian tunneling-burst template to reuse for the pulse model
Reactor antineutrino spectrum input for the CEvNS flux calculation

references.locator: J. Billard et al., J. Phys. G 44, 105101 (2017), arXiv:1612.09035
references.why_it_matters: Published Ge CEvNS reactor rate prediction used as the normalization cross-check

references.locator: Particle Data Group, Review of Particle Physics, cosmic-rays section (sea-level muon flux)
references.why_it_matters: Anchor for the integral sea-level muon rate through the crystal

forbidden_proxies.subject: claim-cevns
forbidden_proxies.proxy: Reporting spectra in deposited energy only without the reconstruction and bandwidth model
forbidden_proxies.reason: The decisive output is the spectrum in reconstructed energy

forbidden_proxies.subject: claim-muon
forbidden_proxies.proxy: Muon spectrum computed without the 50 kHz bandwidth saturation model
forbidden_proxies.reason: Saturation dominates the muon response and omitting it would look like progress while skipping the decisive physics

weakest_anchors: The lumped ~50% deposited-to-signal efficiency replaces the paper's design-dependent efficiency chain
Ta->Al device tunneling parameters are extrapolated rather than tabulated in the QPD paper
unvalidated_assumptions: Uniform phonon-energy sharing among QPD sensors on the crystal
qpd-repo EMG template parameters apply to a 1 kg Ge crystal
disconfirming_observations: Computed total CEvNS rate disagrees with published Ge reactor predictions by more than an order of magnitude
The response chain shows no saturation even when tunneling rates far exceed the 25 kHz Nyquist limit

open_questions: What crystal area is instrumented (one face vs all faces), fixing N_sens from the 1/mm^2 sensor density?
How should reconstruction behave in the saturated regime: simple Nyquist rate-clip or a dead-time model?
How should the Ta->Al device tunneling parameters be mapped from the QPD paper's tabulated Al- and Hf-junction devices?
